extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and philosophy of science; educated general readers
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and analysis of the concepts Space, Time, Matter, Motion, and Force and their epistemological status: how these notions are generated from experience, their relativity to an Unknowable Absolute, and related necessary propositions (e.g., indestructibility of matter, continuity of motion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Space as an abstract of co-existences
rubrics_metrics.description: Our consciousness of Space is a consciousness of co-existent positions; the abstract of all relations of co-existence (Space) is generated from experiences (chiefly tactile) of individual positions and muscular tensions that register resistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains genesis by analysis: imagined boundaries of space are conceived as co-existent positions (blank forms left when realities are absent). The experiences out of which the abstract of co-existences is generated are experiences of individual positions ascertained by touch and muscular resistance. Emphasizes that Space, thus generated, is purely relative and may be accepted as a valid basis for reasoning about relative truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time as analogous relative/conceptual abstraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Conception of Time follows a parallel argument to Space: Time (relative and absolute) is an abstract generated from experiences (in analogous ways to Space) and is relative rather than absolute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author states conclusions about Time are parallel and too obvious to detail; the conception of Time is produced by some mode of the Unknowable and its unchangeableness implies uniformity of effects on us.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matter defined as co-existent positions that offer resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Conception of Matter reduced to co-existent positions that offer resistance (as opposed to Space, whose co-existent positions offer no resistance); resistance is primary, extension secondary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues mentally abstracting co-existent resistances removes consciousness of Body leaving Space. Because different muscular adjustments habitually indicate different co-existent resistent positions, we represent elements of Matter as extended and resistent. Therefore forces (correlations of resistances) form the whole content of our idea of Matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion as synthesis of Space, Time, and Matter derived from force-experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion involves the conceptions of Space, Time, and Matter: series of positions occupied in succession together with co-existent positions; adult idea of Motion is elaborated from experiences of force and muscular tensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental element: the necessity that a moving body continue to change position arises from earliest muscular experiences. Motion, Space, and Time develop simultaneously from multiplied impressions of muscular tension and objective resistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Force as the ultimate primordial datum of consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Force is the ultimate element: Space, Time, Matter, and Motion are built up of or abstracted from experiences of Force; experiences of Force supply materials for forms of relations and the related objects built up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single impressions of force can be received by a sentient being; multiplicity and difference of such impressions give material for thought and relations. The nature of this undecomposable element is inscrutable; force as we know it is a conditioned effect of an Unconditioned Cause and is relative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relativity of our conceptions to an Unknowable Absolute
rubrics_metrics.description: Our conceptions (Space, Time, Matter, Motion, Force) are produced by some mode of the Unknowable; they are relative representations and we cannot legitimately call those modes necessary conditions of the Unknowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We can only assert that the relative realities imply some absolute reality equally unchanging for our concerns; noumenon and phenomenon are two sides of the same change and both should be regarded as real in their relative relation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indestructibility of Matter (as permanence of the force it exerts)
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrine that Matter is indestructible is essential for science: matter cannot be conceived as passing into non-existence; what we really mean by indestructibility is the permanence of the force (resistance/gravitative force) with which Matter affects us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides historical and empirical arguments: apparent creations/annihilations are explained as redistributions or state-changes; quantitative chemistry and weighing presuppose indestructibility; analysis of consciousness shows annihilation/creation are unthinkable because thought requires relations. The permanence of matter is illustrated by permanence of its forces (e.g., weighing, chemical inferences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary physical truths require developed mental structure and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of necessary truths in physics (analogous to logical truths) requires both a mental structure capable of grasping terms and a definite representation of those terms; such necessary truths become cognizable as intelligence develops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a savage unable to count cannot apprehend 7+5=12; a careless boy may err. Similarly, many popular notions betray inability to form clear ideas of forces and their relations. Thus physical axioms can be known a priori by a developed intelligence (a priori here means rendered organic by accumulated ancestral experience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of Motion as necessary postulate for exact science
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuity of Motion (or of whatever has Motion as a sensible form) is a general truth on which the possibility of exact science depends: motions cannot proceed from nothing nor lapse into nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that if motions could arise from or lapse into nothing, scientific interpretation would be impossible because an incalculable element would be introduced; motions of masses and molecules form the larger half of phenomena to be interpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between disappearance from perception and annihilation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a vital distinction between matter vanishing from the range of perception (becoming invisible, diffused, or beyond range) and matter being annihilated (passing into non-existence); confusing these leads to belief in creation/annihilation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives examples: comets discovered growing larger were previously beyond vision, clouds forming are condensation of pre-existing substance, precipitates from liquids, evaporated water recoverable by condensation. Emphasizes need for discrimination to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight/force as the operational measure of quantity of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of matter is operationally determined by the force (gravitative, chemical) it manifests; scientific inferences about quantities of matter rely on permanence and equivalence of these forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighing presumes constancy of the matter weighed; chemical combinations infer quantities from neutralization weights. Thus permanence of force is the empirical basis for indestructibility claims and for following scientific practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic and ether hypotheses as necessary developments of cognitive forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypotheses like the atomic theory or an all-pervading ether are necessary developments of the universal forms produced in us by the Unknowable; conclusions worked out with these hypotheses will have relative truth in harmony with other results implied by the same forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author endorses that using such hypotheses in physical/chemical research is legitimate because they are necessary developments of our experiential forms; their logical conclusions will be relatively true and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought's impossibility to conceive creation or annihilation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is impossible to conceive something becoming nothing or nothing becoming something because thought requires relations between states and nothing cannot be an object of consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is given as an a priori/analytic point: annihilation or creation cannot be objects of thought for the same reason—nothing cannot serve as a term in relations essential for consciousness.
